0.en: Maxims for the Journal of German Literature260)

en: The general purpose is the furthering of scientific and aesthetic culture, in which everyone who does not belong to the trade class takes part through criticism of the new writings appearing in Germany that concern the sciences and art.
zh: 总的目的在于促进科学的与审美的教养，凡不属于行业阶级的人，都通过对在德意志新出的、涉及各门科学和艺术的著作的批判来参与这种教养。

en: a) All essays that do not contain the criticism of a writing are excluded, since their content, on account of the indeterminacy of its circle, becomes too heterogeneous, and in its individuality contains too limited an interest, while in its generality — which on account of the slight execution easily becomes superficiality — it contains too small an interest.
zh: a) 所有不包含对一部著作的批判的文章都被排除在外，因为它们的内容由于它那个范围无法确定而变得过于异质，并且就其个别性说包含着一种过于受限制的兴趣，就其普遍性说——这种普遍性由于缺少展开而很容易变成肤浅——则包含着一种过于微小的兴趣。

en: b) Criticism does not have literary knowledge as its aim, hence neither a complete notice of all writings that appear, which other journals can anyway give more in promise than in reality.
Deliberately, therefore, what is unimportant is partly passed over, partly what does not belong to scientific and fine literature; thus the economic, technological and similar branches are excluded.
zh: b) 批判并不以文学知识为目的，因此也不以完整通告所有出版的著作为目的，何况其他刊物本来也多半只是许诺，而并不真的现实地做到。
所以，人们有意略过一部分不重要的东西，也略过不属于科学的和美文学的那部分；因此，经济的、技术的以及诸如此类的科目都被排除在外。

en: c) The detail of the particular proper sciences — theology, jurisprudence and so forth — likewise stays out of this plan, insofar as it can interest only someone who occupies himself with it exclusively and directly.

But with general works on these sciences, as also on medicine, physics, natural history, chemistry, mathematics, history and philology, whether a criticism of them corresponds to the purpose of this institute cannot depend so much on their content as it depends rather on the manner of this criticism itself, namely whether general spiritual culture as such, and science and taste, gain thereby.
zh: c) 各门特殊的、本来意义上的科学的细节，如神学、法学等等，同样不在这个计划之内，因为这类细节只能让那种专门而直接地从事它的人感兴趣。
但是，对于论述这些科学以及论述医学、物理学、自然史、化学、数学、历史、语文学的一般性著作，对它们的批判是否符合这个机构的目的，与其说取决于它们的内容，不如说取决于这种批判本身的方式，即一般的精神教养本身以及科学和品味是否因此有所收获。

en: d) These are not furthered by what are ordinarily called reviews and judgments, by which a writing is merely characterized but no entry is made into its content, — by which one learns, say, whether the book is good or bad, and the titles that the author treats, but the matter itself is not examined and talked through with him.
Criticisms should therefore have more of the treating kind, in which the author's presentation is taken as the basis and followed, than of the reviewing kind as such.
zh: d) 这些东西不是靠通常所说的书评和评判来促进的，这种书评和评判只是给一部著作描出特征，却并不进入它的内容，——人们从中约略得知这本书是好是坏，得知作者讨论的是哪些题目，但事情本身并没有被考察，也没有同作者一起谈透。
因此，批判与其说应当具有书评式的性质本身，不如说应当具有论述式的性质，也就是把作者的阐述作为基础并顺着它走。

en: e) Insofar as a work — be it of empirical or theoretical content — is so constituted that it indeed shows itself interesting, yet the novelty of its content still permits no proper judgment, a historical exposition of its content (analysis) is to be given and the false shame is to be removed which, because the reviewer does not feel himself able to show himself at it as a master already finished with everything scibili and knowing everything better, prevents it from even being spoken of, as is the case, for example, with [Jacob Joseph] Winterl's and various other writings, in which the reviewers are conscious of not yet being able to swagger and yet will not renounce it and want to be content with an analysis, which for the time being informs the public and is welcome to it and often more welcome than the judgment; if it has only to choose between the two, an analysis and a pure review, the former will certainly be welcome to it.
zh: e) 只要一部著作——不论其内容是经验的还是理论的——是这样一种情况，即它虽然显得有趣，但其内容的新颖还不允许作出真正的评判，那就应当对它的内容作一种历史性的陈述（分析），并消除那种虚假的羞耻，这种羞耻因为书评人觉得自己还没有能力以对一切 scibili 都已了结、并且什么都懂得更多的行家姿态出现在这部著作面前，就阻止人们哪怕只是谈到它，例如[雅各布·约瑟夫]温特尔的以及某些其他著作就是这种情况，而在这些著作上，书评人自己知道还不能摆架子，却又不肯放弃这一点、只满足于一篇分析，而分析暂时能告知公众，是公众所欢迎的，而且往往比评判更受欢迎；如果公众只能在两者之间，也就是一篇分析和一篇纯粹的书评之间作选择，那么前者肯定会让它觉得合意。

en: f) Likewise there is no place for reviews which, with the intention of proving to the author the attention with which his writing has been read, are besides the general judgment a dialogue with the author and make carping objections to him and hand him corrections that are of interest only between the author and the reviewer, but to no third party.
In general, everything falls away that should be merely the personal opinion of the reviewer, even if he thereby gives himself the position of a representative of the public.
zh: f) 同样没有位置的，是那些为了向作者证明他的著作受到了怎样的关注、除了总的评判之外还同作者进行对话、对他吹毛求疵并向他提供更正的书评，而这些更正只在作者与书评人之间才有意义，对任何第三方都没有意义。
总的来说，凡是只应属于书评人个人意见的东西都一概去掉，哪怕他借此把自己摆成公众代表的位置。

en: g) To engage, by contrast, with the essential content of works from certain fields has just as much general interest as it is conducive to science.

To cite a specific example, this would be the case with a review of a book such as Paulus' commentary on the New Testament263), if a review examined its maxims. — In other particular sciences, e.g. jurisprudence, what concerns natural law and public law, also systems of pandects, investigations of criminal justice, Code Napoléon and the like, likewise belong here.
Thus from medicine its systematic part, as well as ingenious views and treatments of individual diseases, yellow fever with its temporary interest, and so forth.
From physics as from chemistry, essentially those works belong here that contain an enrichment of the sciences.

Ancient literature should in any case have the interest of every educated person for itself; it is important to pave and ease the way to it for him, especially by lowering the value of the merely pedantic efforts with it and of the scientiae arcane, whose semblance some who are of the profession give themselves, but which, examined more closely, shows itself to be their whim and arbitrariness.
zh: g) 相反，深入探讨某些学科的著作的本质内容，既有同样普遍的兴趣，也对科学有益。
举一个具体的例子，在评论保卢斯的《新约注释》263)这样一本书时，如果一篇书评考察了它的箴言，情况就会是这样。——在其他特殊的科学中，例如法学，涉及自然法、国家法的东西，还有潘德克顿体系、关于刑事司法的研究、Code Napoléon 之类，同样属于这里。
医学方面则如它的系统部分，又如对个别疾病的富有才智的见解和处理，以及只有一时兴趣的黄热病等等。
物理学和化学方面，本质上属于这里的是那些使各门科学有所丰富的著作。
古代文学本来就应该让每个有教养的人对它感兴趣；重要的是为这种人铺平并便利通向它的道路，尤其是通过贬低在这方面纯粹迂腐的努力以及 scientiae arcane 的价值，后者是某些以这门行当为业的人给自己制造出来的假象，但仔细一看，它不过是他们的怪念头和任意妄为。

en: h) There awaits all the sciences at present a rebirth with regard to their concepts and to the spiritlessness that transforms scientific content into mere material and handles uncritically and unconsciously the concepts that it ordinarily does not even know it has.
The theoretical and empirical side constitutes a tradition that is handed down unexamined, as something long since proved and laid up in the treasury, from one hand to another.
It is against this tradition — which anyway already has, if not the contempt, then at least the boredom of the public against it — that criticism in particular has to direct its investigation.

Precisely that which is current and common, which has custom on its side, which counts as long since known — a kind of old junk, with which usage and, as it were, a conventional way of life bring it about that one lets it pass, without those who keep talking along those lines being really any more in earnest about it than astronomers are when they accommodate themselves to the phrase about the sun's revolving around the earth — precisely this time-honoured stuff most needs to be turned on its head and called into question, in order at first at least to excite astonishment and perplexity, and further to occasion reflection.
zh: h) 目前，各门科学都面临着一场重生，这既是就它们的概念而言，也是就那种无精神状态而言，后者把科学的内容变成纯粹的材料，并无批判地、无意识地摆弄那些它通常根本不知道自己拥有的概念。
理论和经验的一面构成一种传统，这种传统未经审视就被当作早已得到证明的、收进宝库里的东西，从一个人手里传到另一个人手里。
正是针对这种传统——它反正已经招来了公众的厌倦，如果不是蔑视的话——批判尤其要把自己的考察对准它。
正是那种司空见惯、通行无阻、有习俗惯例为它撑腰、并被当作早已知道的东西——一种旧货，习惯和一种近乎约定俗成的生活方式使得人们容忍它、承认它有效，而那些人虽然一直照着它说下去，其实对它并不比对天文学家迁就“太阳绕着地球转”这句老话时更认真——正是这种世代相传、由来已久的东西，最需要被颠倒过来、被追究，以便至少先引起惊奇和错愕，进而促使人去思索。

en: i) What is meant by this is not to enter into the manner of the present fermentation of the sciences, which, starting from philosophy, floods and confuses them.

On the one hand, for the victorious attack on empty and spiritless scientificity, only sound common sense is needed, if it possesses the cultured sureness that will not let itself be confused or impressed by the serious mien of those people.

On the other hand, that philosophical scientificity, which should be an application and the transition of abstract ideas to determinate content and to the proper sciences — which is what is at present to be done — is rather for the most part empty formalism, an unripe brew of half-grasped concepts, shallow and mostly even silly notions, and an ignorance both of philosophy itself and of the sciences, as — to designate more precisely what I mean — the Windischmannian, Görresian, and for the most part also the Steffensian stuff, as well as the samples that the Jena General Literary Gazette gave, especially at its beginning.

It is this raw forest stream, which threatens to confuse reason and science and to whose manners and fundamental propositions Schelling — after having partly stated and used them — now begins solemnly to renounce, that a scientific criticism has above all to oppose itself.

We shall thereby come to the aid of the instinct of the public, which has passed from its first astonishment to an indifference toward that manner, support the respect that is still always basically paid to philosophy on account of its general need, find sympathy among all friends of insight who have been brought to silence and looking away by insolence and immaturity, and disentangle the astonishment that is too timid to examine, which on account of the general ideas woven into that carrying-on had respect for it, and by separating out the impure procure for it the gain of the genuine.
zh: i) 这里说的并不是要跟进当前各门科学那种发酵的做派，这种做派从哲学出发，把它们淹没并搅乱。
一方面，要胜利地攻击空洞而无精神的科学性，只需要健全常识，只要它具有那种有教养的稳妥，不会被那些人的严肃神情弄得不知所措，也不会被它镇住。

另一方面，那种哲学的科学性——它本应是把抽象的观念应用于、并过渡到确定的内容和各门本来意义上的科学，而这正是当前该做的事——却多半是空洞的形式主义，是半生不熟地领会来的概念拼成的未成熟的大杂烩，是浅薄而且大多甚至无聊的念头，是对哲学本身以及对各门科学的无知，具体说来——为了更确切地指明我的意思——就是温迪施曼、格雷斯，还有很大一部分斯蒂芬斯的那套东西，以及《耶拿普通文学报》尤其是它创刊时所提供的样品。
对于这股威胁着要搅乱理性和科学的粗野的森林洪流——谢林在部分地提出并使用过它的做法和根本命题之后，现在正开始郑重地放弃它们——一种科学的批判尤其必须加以抵抗。
这样一来，我们就会帮助公众的本能，这种本能已经从最初的惊奇转为对那种做法的无所谓，就会支持人们由于哲学的普遍需要而始终基本上给予哲学的尊重，就会在所有那些被蛮横和不成熟弄得沉默、转过脸去的有见识的朋友那里得到同情，并且会解开那种胆怯得不敢去检验的惊奇，这种惊奇因为那套装腔作势里编织着的普遍观念而对它怀有敬意，并通过把不纯的东西分离出去，让它获得真正的东西。

en: k) The thorough investigation and the treatment of the matter itself includes of itself that the mediocre and the bad — if it must be spoken of on account of some standing or on account of the pretensions it has — has no forbearance and tolerance to expect, but is surrendered to all grounds against it as well as to wit and to fancies, and likewise that everything personal, everything spiteful, everything that sprang from a pruritus of rubbing or showing oneself, remains excluded.

In the fact that it is the matter that is at stake, this too is contained: that it must be more welcome to the reviewer to be able to recognize something as excellent — with understanding — than to have to speak against it, especially since it is harder to develop properly why something is excellent than to find the defects; but undeveloped admiration and approval has as little interest as mere fault-finding and carping. — Honest zeal for science and thorough treatment remains equally free of the addiction which a reviewer believes he must have, in a certain sense ex officio, of always being cleverer than something already very clever, of knowing how to point out, in the case of the excellent, that it could still have been made better (whereby it would in most cases have become worse), of knowing everything better in general, and of assuming the air of a master and judge with whom there can no longer be any question of his learning something from a piece of writing, and of speaking out of this disposition.
zh: k) 对事情本身作深入的考察和论述，这本身就包含：平庸和低劣的东西——如果由于某种声望，或者由于它抱有的种种自命不凡，不得不谈到它——休想得到任何宽待和宽容，反而要被交给一切反对它的理由，交给机智和灵机；同样也包含：一切涉及个人的东西、一切恶毒的东西，一切出于 pruritus、即出于想自我摩擦或想自我炫耀的东西，都留在外面。

既然要紧的是事情本身，那么这里也就包含：书评人宁可——凭借知性——把某样东西认作卓越的，也不愿不得不反对它，尤其是因为，恰当地展开某样东西为什么卓越，要比找出它的缺点更难；而没有展开的赞赏和称许，其趣味之少，并不亚于单纯的指责和挑剔。——对科学的真诚热忱和深入的论述，同样不沾染这样一种癖好：书评人以为自己多少是职务在身，非得比已经很聪明的东西更聪明不可，在卓越的东西那里还知道指出它本来还可以做得更好（而这样一来，它在多数情况下反倒变得更糟），总之什么都懂得更好，并且摆出一副师傅和法官的架势，仿佛根本谈不上他要从一篇作品里学到什么东西，还从这个意思出发说话。

en: In a word, if — setting aside both personal considerations and the unfounded attachment to what has come down by tradition and to mere opinion, which only asserts and assures, neither examines nor develops — the cause of science and of taste is boldly seized and asserted against all presumptions and maintained with seriousness and penetration into its grounds, then an institute that accomplishes this and thereby distinguishes itself before most of those that exist cannot lack inner interest and interest with the general public, whose instinct always gives the preference to what is right over the bad, with which it puts up for the time being.
zh: 一句话，如果抛开个人的顾虑，也抛开对世代相传的东西的没有根据的依恋，抛开那种只作断言和保证、既不加考察也不加展开的单纯意见，大胆地抓住科学和趣味的事情，针对一切僭妄把它主张出来，并凭着认真态度和对根据的深入来坚持它，那么，一个做到这一点、并因此胜过现有大多数同类机构的机构，就不会缺少内在的趣味，也不会缺少在普通公众那里的趣味，因为公众的直觉总是宁取正当的东西，而不取它暂时还将就着的坏东西。

en: With regard to the external arrangement, I note the following points:
zh: 关于外部的安排，我指出以下几点：

en: The journal appears monthly in instalments of rather 12 than 10 sheets or fewer.
zh: 这份杂志按月出版，每册宁可说是12印张，而不是10印张或更少。

en: The contract with the bookseller is concluded according to the number of copies that are sold, so that 500 or 750 copies are assumed as the definite, fixed starting point and as the minimum.
zh: 与书商的合同按售出的册数来订，所以500册或750册被当作确定的、固定的出发点，也被当作最低数。

en: A directorate, consisting of those who first undertake the institute, conducts the general supervision with regard to the writings to be announced and the collaborators to be invited, and is to be regarded as the owner of the whole.
zh: 一个理事会由最初创办这个机构的人组成，它负责对要评介的著作和要邀请的撰稿人实行总的监督，并被看作整个事业的所有者。

en: The editor, who is a member of the directorate and is permanent, conducts the correspondence, the accounts and the current business of printing, etc.
zh: 编辑是理事会成员，而且是常任的，他负责通信、账目以及印刷等等的日常事务。

en: The costs are first deducted from the proceeds of the whole, then according to the remainder the size of the honoraria is determined, and to the editor, instead of a fixed salary, a certain percentage of the remainder, 15 to 20, is granted for his trouble.
zh: 费用先从整个事业的收益里扣除，再按剩下的余额确定稿酬的数额，并把余额的15到20个百分点判给编辑，作为他辛苦的报酬，以代替固定薪金。

en: The books are supplied by the publishing house at a discount of 20-25 percent of the retail price; the reviewer has the right to keep them at a discount of 40 percent of the same, otherwise the directorate's cash-box sells them.

They are to be counted among the costs. — [Books] which, moreover, have not become unsalable for the bookshop through use, and of which it has not expressly ordered a copy for the institute, and which it can otherwise use, the same takes back again without any commission.
zh: 图书由出版社按定价的20-25%的折扣提供；书评人有权利按同一定价的40%折扣把它们留下，否则就由理事会的账房把它们卖掉。
这些要算进成本。——[图书，]如果在使用中还没有变得让书店卖不出去，如果书店没有专门为这个机构订购过一册，而书店自己还有别的用处，那么书店就把它们收回，不收取任何佣金。

en: The start is made with July 1807.
zh: 从1807年7月开始。

en: Thinking?
Abstract? — Sauve qui peut!
Save himself, whoever can!
Thus I already hear a traitor bought by the enemy cry out, who shouts down this essay on the ground that metaphysics is to be spoken of here.
For metaphysics is the word, as abstract, and almost also thinking, is the word, before which everyone more or less runs away as before one afflicted with the plague.
zh: 思维？
抽象？——Sauve qui peut！
能逃的就逃吧！
我已经听到一个被敌人收买的叛徒这样喊叫，他这样大叫着反对这篇文章，说这里要谈的是形而上学。
因为形而上学就是那个词，正如抽象、几乎还有思维，就是那个词，人人见了它都多多少少像见了染上瘟疫的人一样逃开。

en: But it is not meant so badly that what thinking is and what abstract is should be explained here.
To the beautiful world nothing is so unbearable as explaining.
To me myself it is dreadful enough when someone begins to explain, for at a pinch I understand everything myself.

Here the explanation of thinking and of the abstract showed itself in any case already as completely superfluous; for precisely only because the beautiful world already knows what the abstract is does it flee from it.
As one does not desire what one does not know, so one also cannot hate it.
zh: 不过，这里的意思并没有那么坏，并不是要在这里解释什么是思维、什么是抽象。
对美好的世界来说，没有什么比解释更让人受不了。
对我自己来说，只要有人开始解释，就够让我害怕的了，因为实在不行，我自己什么都懂。
在这里，对思维和对抽象的解释反正已经显得完全多余；因为正是仅仅由于美好的世界已经知道抽象是什么，它才躲开抽象。
正如人不欲求自己不认识的东西，人也不能憎恨它。

en: Nor is it intended to want perfidiously to reconcile the beautiful world with thinking or with the abstract; as if, under the appearance of a light conversation, thinking and the abstract were to be smuggled in, so that it would have crept into society unrecognized, and without having aroused any particular aversion, and had even been drawn in imperceptibly by society itself or, as the Swabians put it, been “fobbed” in, and now the author of this entanglement uncovered this otherwise foreign guest, namely the abstract, whom the whole company had treated and acknowledged under another title as a good acquaintance.

Such scenes of recognition, by which the world is to be instructed against its will, have in themselves the inexcusable fault that they at the same time put to shame, and that the machinist wanted to contrive for himself a little fame, so that that shaming and this vanity cancel the effect, for they rather push away again an instruction bought at this price.
zh: 这里也不想耍阴招，要把美好的世界同思维或抽象调和起来；并不是说，要借一场轻松交谈的样子把思维和抽象夹带进来，好让它在没人认出的情况下，又没有引起什么反感，就溜进社交场合，甚至是被社交场合自己不知不觉地拉进来，或者像施瓦本人说的那样，是被“捎”进来的，然后这场纠葛的作者再把这个本来陌生的客人，也就是抽象，揭出来，而满座的人此前是把它当作一个老熟人、用另一个名目来对待和认可的。
这类相认的场面，本来是要违背世界的意愿去教导它，它们本身有一个不可原谅的毛病：它们既让人羞愧，而设局的人又想给自己勉强造出一点小小的名声，于是那种羞愧和这种虚荣就把效果抵消了，因为这样买来的教导，反而会被它们重新推开。

en: In any case, the laying out of such a plan would already be spoiled; for its execution requires that the solution of the riddle not be pronounced in advance.

But this has already happened through the title; in the title, if this essay were to proceed with such cunning, the words ought not to have appeared right from the start, but, like the minister in the comedy, ought to have walked about in the overcoat throughout the whole play and only in the last scene unbuttoned it and let the star of wisdom flash forth.

The unbuttoning of a metaphysical overcoat would here not even look as good as the unbuttoning of the ministerial one, for what the former would bring to light would be nothing more than a couple of words; for the best part of the jest was really supposed to lie in its showing that the company had long been in possession of the thing itself; so in the end it would gain only the name, whereas the minister's star means something more real, a purse with money.
zh: 再说，这样一份计划的拟定本来就已经被弄糟了；因为要把它付诸实行，就要求谜底不事先说出来。
但这一点通过标题已经发生了；在标题里，如果这篇文章要耍这样的诡计，这些字眼就不该一开始就露面，而应该像喜剧里的那位大臣一样，整出戏都穿着外套走来走去，只在最后一幕才把外套解开，让智慧之星闪出来。
在这里，解开一件形而上学的外套，看起来甚至还不如解开那位大臣的外套体面，因为前者亮出来的，无非是几个字眼；这个玩笑最妙的地方本来就在于，它表明在座的人早就占有着事情本身了；所以它到头来只赢得一个名称，而那位大臣的星章却意味着某种更实在的东西，一个装钱的袋子。

en: What thinking is, what is abstract — that every person present knows this is presupposed in good society, and we are in such society.
The only question is who it is that thinks abstractly.

The intention is, as already recalled, not that of reconciling it with these things, not that of expecting it to busy itself with something difficult, not that of speaking to its conscience about its frivolously neglecting something that would be in keeping with the rank and station of a being endowed with reason.

Rather, the intention is to reconcile the beautiful world with itself about this, if indeed it does not make a conscience for itself about this neglect, but yet at least inwardly has a certain respect for abstract thinking as for something high and looks away from it, not because it is too lowly for it but because it is too high, not because it is too common but too distinguished, or conversely, because abstract thinking seems to it to be an espèce, something particular, something by which one does not distinguish oneself in general society, as by a new finery, but by which one rather, as by shabby clothing or also by rich clothing, even if this consists of old-set precious stones or of however rich an embroidery, which however has long become Chinese, excludes oneself from society or makes oneself ridiculous in it.
zh: 什么是思维，什么是抽象——这一点在座每个人都懂得，这是上流社会里预先假定的，而我们就处在这样的社会里。
问题只在于，到底是谁在抽象地思维。
正如已经提过的那样，目的并不是要让它与这些东西和解，不是要指望它去跟什么困难的东西打交道，也不是要就它轻率地忽略了某种东西这一点去跟它的良心讲话，而那种东西对一个赋有理性的存在者来说本是合乎其身份和等级的。

相反，目的是要让这美好的世界在这件事上同自己和解，如果它本来并不为这种忽视而良心不安，却毕竟对抽象思维作为某种高深的东西至少内心里还怀有几分敬意，并且对它避开不看，不是因为它太微不足道，而是因为它太高，不是因为它太卑下，而是因为它太高贵，或者反过来，因为在它看来，抽象思维是一种 Espèce（特殊种类），某种特别的东西，一种并不能像一套新行头那样让人在一般社交场合里出众的东西，反倒是一种像破旧衣服、或者也像华丽衣服那样让人把自己排除在社会之外、或者在社交场合里成为笑柄的东西——哪怕这衣服镶的是老式镶嵌的宝石，或者绣工再华丽，却早已变得中国式了。

en: Who thinks abstractly?
The uneducated person, not the educated one.

Good society therefore does not think abstractly, because it is too easy, because it is too low — low not in respect of external station, not out of an empty putting on of airs that sets itself above what it is incapable of, but on account of the inner pettiness of the matter.
zh: 谁在抽象地思维？
没有教养的人，而不是有教养的人。
上流社会之所以不抽象地思维，是因为这太容易，是因为这太低，这低不是就外在的身份来说的，不是出于一种空洞的摆架子，这种摆架子硬要凌驾于它所做不到的东西之上，而是因为事情本身内在的渺小。

en: The prejudice in favour of and the respect for abstract thinking is so great that fine noses will here scent a satire or an irony in advance; but since they are readers of the Morgenblatt265), they know that a prize has been set on a satire, and that I would therefore rather believe that I am to earn it and compete for it than give away my things here already without further ado.
zh: 对抽象思维的偏见和敬重是如此之大，以至于嗅觉灵敏的人在这里会事先嗅出一篇讽刺或反讽；不过，既然他们是《晨报》265)的读者，他们就知道，对讽刺作品是悬了奖的，因此我与其在这里就把我的东西随随便便交出去，倒宁愿相信自己能挣到它、并为此去竞争。

en: For my proposition I need only adduce examples of which everyone will admit that they contain it.
So a murderer is led to the place of execution.
To the common people he is nothing more than a murderer.
Ladies perhaps remark that he is a strong, handsome, interesting man.
Those people find the remark appalling: what, a murderer handsome? how can one be so wicked in one's thinking as to call a murderer handsome; you are probably not much better either!
This is the corruption of morals that prevails among the genteel people, the priest perhaps adds, who knows the ground of things and the hearts of men.
zh: 为我的命题，我只需要举出例子，而每个人都会承认这些例子包含着它。
于是，一个杀人犯被押往刑场。
在普通百姓眼里，他不过是个杀人犯。
女士们也许会说，他是个强壮、英俊、有趣的男人。
那些百姓觉得这个说法可怕极了：什么，一个杀人犯还英俊？一个人怎么能心思坏到这种地步，竟说一个杀人犯英俊；你们恐怕也好不到哪里去！
这就是在上等人中间流行的道德败坏，教士也许会补上一句，他懂得事物的根据，也懂得人心。

en: A connoisseur of human nature traces the course that the criminal's upbringing has taken, finds in his story a bad education, bad family circumstances of the father and the mother, some monstrous harshness on the occasion of a lighter offence of this man, which embittered him against the civil order, a first reaction against it, which drove him out of it and made it possible for him now to keep himself going only through crimes. — There may well be people who, when they hear such things, will say: he wants to excuse this murderer!

Indeed I recall having heard, in my youth, a mayor complain that the book-writers carry things too far and seek to root out Christianity and uprightness entirely; someone had written a defence of suicide; dreadful, all too dreadful! — It turned out on further inquiry that Werther's Leiden was what was meant.
zh: 一个善于看人的人会去追查这个罪犯的教养所走过的历程，在他的经历里找到糟糕的教育、父亲和母亲糟糕的家庭关系、这个人因一次较轻的过错而遭到的某种骇人的严酷，这种严酷使他对市民秩序积下了怨恨，找到由此产生的第一次反作用，这种反作用把他从市民秩序里赶了出去，使他如今只有靠犯罪才能保住自己。——恐怕会有些人，听到这些就说：他这是想替这个杀人犯开脱！
我确实还记得，我年轻时听到一位市长抱怨说，那些写书的人搞得太远，一心要把基督教和正直彻底铲除；说有个人写了一篇替自杀辩护的东西；可怕，实在太可怕了！——再一打听才弄清楚，原来指的是《维特之烦恼》。

en: This means thinking abstractly: to see in the murderer nothing but this abstract thing, that he is a murderer, and through this simple quality to extinguish in him all the remaining human essence.
Quite otherwise a fine, sensitive Leipzig world.
It strewed and bound the wheel and the criminal who was woven onto it with wreaths of flowers. — But this is again the opposite abstraction.
Christians may well carry on Rosicrucianism, or rather cross-rosing, winding the cross with roses.
The cross is the long-since consecrated gallows and wheel.

It has lost its one-sided meaning of being the instrument of dishonouring punishment, and on the contrary knows the representation of the highest pain and the deepest rejection together with the most joyful bliss and divine honour.
By contrast the Leipzig [cross], bound round with violets and corn-roses, is a Kotzebuean reconciliation, a kind of slovenly compatibility of sentimentality with the bad.
zh: 这就叫抽象地思维：在杀人犯身上只看见这个抽象的东西，即他是个杀人犯，并凭借这个单纯的性质，把他身上其余的一切人性都抹掉。
一个优雅而多情的莱比锡世界则完全是另一副样子。
它给轮子和被绑缚在轮子上的罪犯撒上花环、缠上花环。——但这又是相反的那种抽象。
基督徒尽可以搞他们的玫瑰十字，或者不如说是十字玫瑰，用玫瑰把十字架缠绕起来。
十字架是早已被奉为神圣的绞架和轮刑架。
它已经失去了自己那个片面的含义，即充当使人蒙受耻辱的刑罚的工具，相反，它知道最高的痛苦和最深的弃绝的表象，连同最欢快的极乐和神的荣耀。
相反，莱比锡的〔十字架〕，用紫罗兰和虞美人缠绑起来，是一种科策布式的和解，是感伤情怀与恶劣东西之间一种随随便便的相容。

en: Quite differently I once heard a common old woman, a hospital woman, kill the abstraction of the murderer and make him alive to honour.

The severed head had been laid on the scaffold, and there was sunshine; how very beautiful, she said, God's sun of grace shines upon Binder's head! - You are not worthy that the sun shine on you, one says to a wretch with whom one is angry.
That woman saw that the murderer's head was shone upon by the sun and was therefore still worthy of it.

She raised him from the punishment of the scaffold into the sun-grace of God, did not bring about the reconciliation through her violets and her sentimental vanity, but saw him received into grace in the higher sun.
zh: 完全以另一种方式，我从前听见一个普通的老妇人、一个济贫院的女人，把凶手这个抽象杀死，让他活过来、重获荣誉。
那颗被砍下的头已经放在断头台上，而且有阳光；她说，上帝的恩典之阳把宾德尔的头照得多么美啊！——对一个让自己发火的卑贱家伙，人们就说：你不配让太阳照你。
那个妇人看到，凶手的头被太阳照着，因此也还配得上这阳光。
她把他从断头台的刑罚提升到上帝的太阳恩典里，不是靠她的紫罗兰和她那多愁善感的虚荣促成了和解，而是看见他在那更高的太阳里被接纳进恩典。

en: Old woman, your eggs are rotten, says the buyer to the huckster woman.
What, she retorts, my eggs rotten?
She may be rotten herself, for all I care!
She presumes to say that about my eggs?
She?

Did the lice not eat up her father on the highway, did her mother not run off with the French and her grandmother die in the hospital, - let her buy herself a whole shirt for her tinsel neckerchief; one knows well where she got this neckerchief and her caps; if the officers were not there, many a one would not be so decked out now, and if the fine ladies looked more after their housekeeping, many a one would be sitting in the house of correction, - let her just mend the holes in her stockings! - In short, she leaves no good thread on her.

She thinks abstractly and subsumes her, according to neckerchief, cap, shirt etc. as according to fingers and other parts, also according to the father and the whole clan, quite alone under the crime that she found the eggs rotten; everything about her is dyed through and through with these rotten eggs, whereas those officers of whom the huckster spoke - if indeed, as is very much to be doubted, there is anything in it - may get to see quite other things in her.
zh: “老太婆，你的蛋是臭的，”女买主对小贩女人说。
“什么，”她回嘴说，“我的蛋臭？”
她自己才臭，随她去！
她竟敢这样说我的蛋？
她？
她父亲不是让虱子在公路边吃掉了，她母亲不是跟着法国人跑了，她祖母不是死在济贫院里，——那就让她拿她那块亮片围巾去给自己换一件完整的衬衫吧；人们很清楚她这块围巾和她的那些帽子是从哪儿来的；要不是有那些军官，如今有些女人也不会打扮得这么光鲜，要是那些尊贵的太太们多照看照看自己的家务，有些女人早就蹲在管教所里了，——让她先去补补自己袜子上的窟窿吧！——总之，她没在她身上留下一根好线。
她在抽象地思维，按照围巾、帽子、衬衫等等，也按照手指和其他部位，还按照父亲和整个家族，把她完全只归到那桩罪行之下，即她发现那些蛋是臭的；她身上的一切都被这些臭蛋染透了，相反，女贩子所说的那些军官——倘若这里头真有什么东西，而这是大可怀疑的——在她身上也许看到的是完全另外一些东西。

en: To come from the maid to the manservant: no servant is worse off than with a man of little rank and little income, and the better off he is the more distinguished his master is.
The common man again thinks more abstractly: he puts on airs toward the servant and relates to him only as to a servant; he holds fast to this one predicate.
The servant is best off with the French.

The distinguished man is familiar with the servant, the Frenchman is even a good friend to him; the servant, when they are alone, does the talking - see Diderot's Jacques et son maître - the master does nothing but take snuff and look at the clock and lets the servant have his way in everything else.

The distinguished man knows that the servant is not only a servant but also knows the town news, is acquainted with the girls, has good plans in his head; he asks him about it, and the servant may say what he knows about that which the principal asked about.

With the French master the servant may not only do this, but also bring the matter up, have and assert his own opinion, and if the master wants something, it does not go by command, but he must first reason his opinion into the servant and give him a good word for it, so that his opinion keeps the upper hand.
zh: 从女仆说到男仆：没有哪个仆人的处境比在一位地位低、收入少的男人那里更糟，而主人越是显贵，他的处境就越好。
普通人又想得更抽象：他对仆人摆出老爷的架子，只把仆人当作仆人对待；他抓住这一个谓词不放。
仆人在法国人那里过得最好。
尊贵的人对仆人很随和，法国人甚至跟他交朋友；他们单独在一起时，说话算数的是仆人——可参看狄德罗的 Jacques et son maître（《雅克和他的主人》）——主人除了吸鼻烟、看怀表什么也不做，其余一切全让仆人自己做主。
尊贵的人知道，仆人不只是仆人，他还知道城里的新闻，认识那些姑娘，脑子里有不错的主意；主人就这些事问他，仆人也可以说出，对主人所问的事他知道些什么。
在法国主人那里，仆人不仅可以这样，还可以把事情摆到桌面上，有自己的意见并坚持它；主人若想要什么，也不是靠命令，而是得先向仆人把自己的意见讲通，还要为此说句好话，他的意见才占上风。

en: In the military the same difference occurs; under the Prussian one the soldier can be beaten, so he is a canaille; for what has the passive right to be beaten is a canaille.

Thus the common soldier counts to the officer as this abstraction of a beatable subject, with which a gentleman who has uniform and Porte d'épée must deal, and that is, to surrender oneself to the devil.
zh: 军队里也有同样的区别；在普鲁士军队里，士兵可以被抽打，所以他是个下贱东西；因为凡是有挨打的被动权利的，就是下贱东西。
于是普通士兵在军官眼里就是这样一个抽象，即一个可以挨打的主体，一个有制服和 Porte d'épée 的老爷不得不与之打交道的东西，而这就是——把自己交给魔鬼。

40.en: Hegel's Curriculum Vitae in His Own Hand266)

en: [Draft of September 1804]
zh: [1804年9月的草稿]

en: I, Ge[org] W[ilhelm] Fr[iedrich] H[egel], born
Stuttgart 27.
Aug.
My parents G[eorg] L[udwig] Hegel, Rentk[ammer]-Exp[editions]-Rat, and Ch[ristine] L[uise], née

Piously they cared for my education in the sciences both through private instruction and through the public instruction of the Gymnasium at Stuttgart, where the ancient and modern languages as well as the rudiments of the sciences were taught.
I was, in the 18th
year, admitted into the theological seminary at Tübingen.

After two years, which were spent on the study of philology under Schn[urrer] and of philosophy and mathematics under Flatt and Beckh, I became Master of Philosophy and thereupon studied the theological sciences for three years under Le Bret, Uhland, Storr and Flatt, until I had passed the theological examination before the Consistory in Stuttgart and was admitted among the candidates of theology; I had taken up the office of preacher according to my parents' wish and had remained faithful to the study of theology out of inclination, for the sake of its connection with classical literature and philosophy.

After I had been admitted, I chose among the professions of the theological estate the one which, independent of the actual professional labours, of the business of the preaching office, granted me as much leisure to devote myself to ancient literature and philosophy as it afforded the opportunity to live in other countries under foreign circumstances.

I found these in the two private-tutor positions which I accepted in Bern and in Frankfurt, whose professional business left me time enough to follow the course of the science that I had made the determination of my life.

After 6 years, which I spent on both, and after the death of my father, I resolved to devote myself entirely to philosophical science, and the fame of Jena left no choice about the place, where I would find opportunity both to cultivate most beautifully what I had worked out for myself and to try the teaching office.

I wrote here a treatise on the Difference between Fichte's and Schelling's Systems of Philosophy, [on] the inadequacy of the former, and thereupon soon obtained permission from the curators through the public defence of my dissertation de orbitis planetarum.
Together with Prof. Schelling I published the Critical Journal of Philosophy in two volumes, in which [by me]:
zh: 我，格[奥尔格]·威[廉]·弗[里德里希]·黑[格尔]，生于
斯图加特 27.
8月
我的父母格[奥尔格]·路[德维希]·黑格尔，税务署文书参事，和克[里斯蒂娜]·路[易丝]，娘家姓
他们虔诚地为我的科学教育操心，既通过私人授课，也通过斯图加特中学的公开授课，那里教授古代语言和现代语言以及各门科学的基础知识。
我在第18
年进入图宾根的神学院。
两年之后，这两年用来在施努[雷尔]门下学语文学、在弗拉特和贝克门下学哲学和数学，我成了哲学硕士，接着又在勒布雷、乌兰德、施托尔和弗拉特门下学了三年神学，直到我在斯图加特的教会监理会面前通过了神学考试、被录取为神学候补者；我是按父母的愿望选择了布道这一行，并且出于爱好一直忠实于神学学习，为的是它与古典文学和哲学的联系。
被录取之后，我在神学身份的各种职业中选择了那样一种：它不依赖于本来的职业工作、不依赖于布道事务，既给我足够的闲暇可以献身于古代文学和哲学，又给我机会到别的国家、在陌生的境况中生活。
我在伯尔尼和法兰克福接受的两个家庭教师职位上找到了这种机会：那些职务上的事情给我留下足够的时间，让我能够跟随那门我已定为自己人生使命的科学的进程。
我在这两处共度过6年，父亲去世之后，我决定完全献身于哲学科学，而耶拿的声誉使我在地方上无可选择——在那里我既能找到机会，把我为自己所做的工作最美好地加以培养，也能试一试教书这一行。
我在这里写了一篇关于《费希特与谢林哲学体系的差别》的文章，讲的是前者的不充分，随后不久就通过公开答辩我的论文 de orbitis planetarum 而从校方主管那里获得了许可。
我与谢林教授共同出版了《哲学批判杂志》，共两卷，其中[有我写的]：

en: The Introduction, How the Common Human Understanding Takes Philosophy, On the Old and the Newer Scepticism, The Kantian, Jacobian and Fichtean Philosophy, The Previous Treatment of Natural Law.
zh: 《导论》，《普通人的常识怎样看待哲学》，《论古代的与较新的怀疑论》，《康德、雅可比和费希特哲学》，《迄今对自然法的处理》。

en: For three years a Privatdozent of philosophy, I have held various lectures on it, and I believe, last winter before a numerous audience.
The Ducal Mineralogical Society admitted me last year as second assessor, the natural-research society recently as its member.
zh: 我做哲学私人讲师已经三年，讲过好几门关于哲学的课，而且我相信，去年冬天是在人数众多的听众面前讲的。
公爵的矿物学学会去年接纳我为第二评议员，自然研究学会前不久接纳我为它的会员。

en: Since the science of philosophy has thus become my vocation amid manifold studies, I cannot do otherwise than have the wish to be appointed by the Most Serene Patrons as public teacher of it.
zh: 既然在多方面的研究中，哲学这门科学就这样成了我的职业，那我也就不能不抱有这个愿望，就是由最尊贵的庇护者们任命我为它的公开教师。
